recipes.name: Loaded Greek Burgers
ingredients_raw: 8 ounces fresh spinach - rinsed, drained and coarsely chopped
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Make the spread: Stir feta cheese, mayonnaise, lime juice, mint, and parsley together in a small bowl. Set aside until needed.
Make the burgers: Preheat the oven's broiler and set the oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Cut bell pepper in half from top to bottom; remove stem, seeds, and ribs. Place pepper onto the prepared baking sheet with the cut sides facing down.
Cook under the preheated broiler until the skin has blackened and blistered, about 5 minutes. Remove from the oven and transfer pepper halves to a paper bag to cool and steam, about 5 minutes.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat, and lightly oil the grate.
Peel and discard bell pepper skin. Dice flesh and place into a large bowl.

Add ground beef, spinach, feta, bread crumbs, onion, egg, garlic, mint, basil, parsley, salt, and pepper; mix gently with your hands until evenly combined. Form meat mixture into four 4 1/2-inch-diameter patties.

Cook on the preheated grill until the burgers are cooked to your desired degree of doneness, about 4 minutes per side for medium. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).
Serve burgers on warm rolls with feta cheese spread, fresh tomatoes, and lettuce.

raw_recipe.headline: Loaded Greek Burgers
raw_recipe.description: Instead of plain burgers at your next summer cookout, try this Greek burger recipe with fresh herbs, spinach, roasted red peppers, and a tangy feta spread.

review.reviewBody: I made these this summer for my friends and they were a huge hit! Make sure to serve them with the Tzatziki sauce.

Made this as a low carb meal (no bun) and it was great! Used frozen burgers (no meat to make fresh) in our Ninja grill. Added a bit of Greek dressing to burgers before cooking and it added even more flavor! Topped burgers with the feta sauce, spinach, cut up cherry tomatoes and roasted pepper! Will definitely make again!

Great recipe! I used a 10 oz. box of frozen spinach (thawed and squeezed dry) and my son requested meatloaf instead of burgers so I just mixed up the meat mixture and put it in a loaf pan, baked for about 1 - 1 1/4 hours. I also made the spread for us to put on the meatloaf as we plated it. Great will definitely make again!

I don't typically like just a big hunk of meat, so I was searching for a way to add more veggies and flavor to a boring old burger. These turned out great! I had a ton of feta left over from something else, so I used a bit more than what was called for in both the meat and sauce. I also subbed sour cream for the mayo in the sauce because I didn't have any. I would definitely make these again.

I love this recipe!! I went with what I had in my fridge, so I got a little creative! I used half lamb & half beef. I didn’t have lime, so I used lemon, which was ok, lime would be better. I also used grilled onions because I had leftovers- and they were tasty with the red pepper. I didn’t have spinach either, it didn’t matter, flavor wise, but I would like to try it with next time. The flavors really “pop” especially with the sauce!!

This was so easy and tasted great. I used frozen spinach (thawed and squeezed dry) and I used a small jar of roasted red peppers from the store. This cut out a lot of prep time. Plus one pound of meat made 5 large burgers. Next time we will make 6 patties out of it. Very hearty meal. It even stuffed my husband.

I made the following changes: frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed mostly dry, shredded mozzarella, and a large shallot in place of the onion. Also, I only used 1 sprig each of mint and basil. These were pretty decent, very juicy burgers. If anything, I under seasoned them, so they were a bit bland, but nothing a little seasoned salt won't fix. Served one patty over sliced tomatoes and cucumbers with a large dollop of artichoke jalapeno dip over all. Great lunch!

Way too many ingredients for a fairly flavorless burger. The only ingredient that really made any difference to the flavor was the mint. I ended up wanting to have another meal right after making these burgers, just to have some actual taste in my mouth.

Really good my husband and I both liked it I followed the reciepes with no changes. My husband suggested turning it into a meatloaf for a change. I think that’s what I will do, nothing to loose.
Teri
These sounded amazing to me. However, I didn't find them that way. I don't know if it was just my personal taste for feta, but I found that it had too strong of a flavour.

So good!! I don't like peppers so I excluded them, and I added chopped kalamata olives, but I had everything else on hand and it was wonderful! Very thankful I got to use the 3 herbs I grow in this so I didn't have to buy all three. Oh, and it made 6 good size burgers.

Turned out really well. I used ground turkey instead which wasn't as flavorful but the rest of the ingredients were awesome. The sauce wasn't as good, needed more seasoning which I added to taste. Will definitely make again though!

My burgers fell apart on the grill a bit (probably too much stuff, not finely chopped enough and not enough meat in mine), but they are frickin' delicious! I was pleasantly surprised by the mint. I was wary but it adds just the right touch of...something.

12/27/216 - Made the burgers but not the sauce, excellent flavor and presentation! 6/8/14 - Made burgers, left off the mayo sauce - was amazing! So moist and flavorful and delicious! Looks great on the plate, too! I made a double batch and froze half for next time! Love!

I would recommend either cutting down on the spinach (about 4 oz) or increasing the amount of beef (1 1/4-1 1/2 pounds) or possibly both. Either way this will yield more burgers (we got 5 out of the original recipe). Additionally, we only used 6 oz of spinach and 5 oz of feta in the burgers and they completely fell apart. Again, I have no complaints about the taste (amazing!), but this recipe may be much better suited to a meatloaf.
Delicious! We used plain greek yogurt in place of the mayo for a tzaziki sauce. We also used jarred roasted red peppers to make this easier. Great recipe!
